abstract:
BACKGROUND: PIWI-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) have been implicated in tumor biology, but the roles of piRNA-annotated small RNAs in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the cellular effects and molecular associations of piR-016176, a piRNA-annotated small-RNA candidate, in PDAC.
METHODS: Array-based profiling was performed in 10 paired PDAC and adjacent tissues, followed by qRT-PCR validation in an independent cohort of 50 paired specimens. Gain- and loss-of-function assays evaluated cellular phenotypes, while quantitative proteomics and bidirectional rescue experiments assessed the contribution of SAP18. PIWIL1 RIP-qPCR, exploratory acetylome profiling following SAP18 depletion, and integrated transcriptomic-proteomic analysis following piR-016176 overexpression were also performed.
RESULTS: The sequence annotated as piR-016176 showed significantly lower abundance in PDAC tissues and cell lines. Mimic transfection reduced cell viability, wound closure, and Matrigel invasion while increasing apoptosis; inhibitor treatment produced opposite effects. SAP18 protein abundance changed reciprocally, and bidirectional rescue experiments supported its contribution to cell viability and Matrigel invasion. Following mimic transfection, piR-016176 and SAP18 mRNA were enriched in PIWIL1 immunoprecipitates. SAP18 depletion yielded 185 nominally altered acetylome features, none significant after multiple-testing correction, with associated proteins enriched for RNA-regulatory and mitochondrial metabolic functions. Integrating transcriptomic and proteomic data identified 112 concordantly upregulated targets enriched for interferon- and immune-related gene sets after piR-016176 overexpression.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings identify piR-016176 as a piRNA-annotated small-RNA candidate that modulates PDAC cell phenotypes, with SAP18 contributing to its effects on cell viability and Matrigel invasion. PIWIL1-associated RNA enrichment and exploratory acetylome and interferon-related signatures provide additional molecular clues for future investigation. Although its endogenous identity as a mature PIWI-associated piRNA remains to be established, these findings offer a foundation for further characterization of piR-016176 and its associated regulatory mechanisms in PDAC.
key_points_ko: 10쌍의 췌장암 및 인접 조직 조직 아레이 및 50쌍의 독립 코호트 검증에서 piR-016176의 발현이 췌장암에서 유의하게 감소함을 확인했습니다.
piR-016176 모방체(mimic) 주입 시 세포 생존력 및 침윤이 줄어들고 세포사멸이 증가한 반면, 억제제 처리 시 반대 현상이 관찰되었습니다.
piR-016176 과발현 후 전사체 및 단백질체 통합 분석을 통해 인터페론 및 면역 관련 경로에 포함되는 112개의 일치된 상향 조절 표적을 발견했습니다.
summary_ko: 본 연구는 췌장관선암(PDAC)에서 PIWI 상호작용 RNA(piRNA) 후보물질인 piR-016176의 세포학적 영향과 분자 기전을 조사했습니다. 분석 결과 piR-016176은 췌장암 조직 및 세포주에서 발현이 유의하게 낮게 나타났습니다. piR-016176을 세포에 과발현시키면 암세포의 생존력, 이동성, 침윤성이 감소하고 세포사멸이 증가했습니다. 또한 이러한 작용 기전에는 하위 단백질인 SAP18이 관여하는 것으로 확인되었습니다.
title: The piR-016176 candidate small RNA modulates pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cell phenotypes with SAP18 as a functional downstream effector
title_ko: SAP18을 하위 효과 인자로 하여 췌장관선암 세포 형질을 조절하는 piR-016176 후보 소형 RNA에 관한 연구
